fire: Sales reached 4.2 million units last year, up 8 percent from 2019.
The town now has 12,000 residents, down from about 15,000 a decade ago.
Profits rose to $50 million, compared to a $30 million loss the year before.
Unemployment fell to 4.1 percent, down from 5.3 percent in January.
The farm produced 900 tons of wheat, an increase of 12 percent from last season.
Average rent climbed to $1,800, up from $1,500 two years earlier.
Enrollment dropped to 3,400 students, compared with 3,900 the previous fall.
Exports grew 6 percent from the first quarter, the agency said.
